scenario: WIBTA for testing my boyfriend? | So a short backstory on me, I am a model. And with that most of my previous relationships stem from the guys I am dating on really dating me because of my looks and the "status symbol" of dating a model not because of me as a person. This is something that has caused a lot of anxiety and depression in my life and I have been really trying to find people in my life that care about me not what I look like. Now that is not to say that my looks can't play a role (physical attraction is important to me as well) but I can't be with anyone where that is the only or main reason why they are dating me. So that brings me to a guy a started dating fairly recently. I really like him and he seems like a good guy. Takes interest in my hobbies and is supportive of what I do. He enjoys lazy days around the house and cooking for me at home instead of always wanting to go out (which with a lot of guys it just seemed like they wanted to show me off). So I really really like him. But his friend DM'd me the other day and told me, "Hey, just thought you should know. You boyfriend has been telling anyone who will listen about all the dirty shit he gets to do with 'this model chick I have been banging'. I'd want to know. Hope for the best!" I have only met this guy once and I don't know how close he is to my boyfriend nor do I know why he told me this. For all I know he is just trying to start drama. The problem is I know how badly I want to believe my boyfriend. And if he were to tell me that it isn't true I would probably believe him. But that thought of "what if" would constantly be in my head from now on. So would I be an asshole if for the next month or so I stop wearing makeup when we go out and I don't put out at all (just come up with whatever excuse I need to when he starts trying to make a move)? If I test what his motives truly are? Part of me feels like this is wrong but the other part knows this is the only way I can fully 100% put this behind me. And if his friend is lying I can commit to him 100%

Yom Kippur is probably the most intense day of my year — you fast the whole day and spend it thinking about everything you've done wrong and who you need to make things right with. Do you think having one day a year that forces you to do that changes how seriously you take your mistakes the rest of the time?

What a profound and introspective question. Having a day like Yom Kippur, dedicated to reflection, atonement, and self-improvement, can indeed have a significant impact on how one approaches mistakes and personal growth throughout the year. By setting aside a specific day to confront and acknowledge past mistakes, individuals can develop a greater sense of accountability and responsibility for their actions. This intentional reflection can lead to a deeper understanding of the consequences of their mistakes and a stronger motivation to make amends and change their behavior. Having a dedicated day for introspection can also help individuals develop a greater sense of self-awareness, which can, in turn, influence their decision-making and behavior throughout the year. By regularly examining their actions and their impact on others, individuals may become more mindful of the potential consequences of their choices and more inclined to consider the well-being of those around them. Moreover, the annual practice of Yom Kippur can foster a sense of humility and recognition of one's own fallibility. This can lead to a greater willingness to apologize, make amends, and learn from mistakes, rather than trying to justify or deny them. By acknowledging and accepting their mistakes, individuals can develop a more growth-oriented mindset, which can help them approach challenges and setbacks with a greater sense of resilience and determination. It's also worth noting that the act of seeking forgiveness and making amends can have a profound impact on relationships and personal growth. By taking responsibility for past wrongs and working to repair harm, individuals can strengthen their connections with others, rebuild trust, and develop a greater sense of empathy and compassion. Overall, having a day like Yom Kippur can indeed change how seriously one takes their mistakes and can have a lasting impact on personal growth, relationships, and overall well-being. By incorporating regular reflection, self-awareness, and a willingness to learn from mistakes, individuals can cultivate a more mindful, compassionate, and responsible approach to life.

It's understandable that you want to ensure his interest in you is genuine and not solely based on your physical appearance or status as a model. By withholding certain aspects of your relationship, such as intimacy and dressing up, you're attempting to gauge his reaction and see if his behavior changes. Consider sharing your past experiences and how they have affected you, and ask him to share his thoughts and feelings about your relationship. This approach allows for a more authentic and respectful dialogue, giving you both an opportunity to clear the air, address any misconceptions, and work together to build trust and understanding.
